game.name: Texas Hold'em
game.description: Texas Hold'em is a poker game. Each player holds two private cards and shares five cards with the whole table.

vocabulary.means: It names the two private cards a player holds. The word hand names the five cards a player makes at the showdown, so the two words must stay apart.
It names the five cards face up in the middle of the table. The table is the furniture and the group of players, so the two words must stay apart.
It names the disc that marks the seat counted as the dealer. The dealer is the person who gives out the cards, and that person is often not a player.

textFields.describes: how the card is written in hand notation

statFields.describes: The order of the rank, from 2 for a Two to 14 for an Ace. A higher number beats a lower one. An Ace also counts as 1 in the low straight.
The one letter that stands for the suit in hand notation, such as s for Spades.

tokens.syntax: [As] for the ace of spades, or [Kh] for the king of hearts. The first letter is the rank, the second letter is the suit.

answer: The order of the betting rounds, and who acts first in each one.
Which hand beats which, and how a tie divides the pot.
How the dealer builds the main pot and every side pot.
What happens after a dead hand, a misdeal, an exposed card, or an action out of turn.

Odds, probability, equity, outs, pot odds, and any other number that describes a chance of winning.

Bankroll advice, stake selection, and any guidance on gambling money.

extraGuidance: This assistant states the rules. It does not advise how to play. A question that asks what a player should do gets a refusal and a pointer to the rule that says what a player may do.

Texas Hold'em uses one standard pack of 52 cards, so this corpus holds no card database and the card tools are switched off. A question about a single card is a question about the rules of rank and suit, and rule 100.1 answers it.
The word hand carries two meanings at a poker table: the whole deal from the blinds to the showdown, and the best five cards a player makes. Say which one you mean every time you use it.
Table stakes, blind sizes, and rake are house settings. This rulebook states the structure. It does not state the stakes of any one game.
